rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.115(b); Tex. Penal Code § 12.35
rows.notes: In Texas, possessing less than 1 gram of a Penalty Group 1 or 1-B drug (such as heroin, cocaine, meth or fentanyl) is a state jail felony: 180 days to 2 years in state jail and a fine up to $10,000.
rows.issue: Values correct. Texas grades drugs by Penalty Group, not federal schedule; 'Schedule I' label is a mislabel for Penalty Group 1 (heroin, cocaine, meth) / 1-B (fentanyl).

rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.115(c); Tex. Penal Code § 12.34
rows.notes: Possessing 1 gram to under 4 grams of a Penalty Group 1 or 1-B drug is a third-degree felony in Texas: 2 to 10 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000.
rows.issue: Values correct; 'Schedule I' label should be Penalty Group 1/1-B.

rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.115(d); Tex. Penal Code § 12.33
rows.notes: Possessing 4 grams to under 200 grams of a Penalty Group 1 or 1-B drug is a second-degree felony in Texas: 2 to 20 years in prison and a fine up to $10,000.
rows.issue: App said 5-99 years (first-degree range); a second-degree felony is 2-20 years.

rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.115(e)-(f); Tex. Penal Code § 12.32
rows.notes: Possessing 200 grams to under 400 grams of a Penalty Group 1 or 1-B drug is a first-degree felony: 5 to 99 years or life and a fine up to $10,000. At 400 grams or more the range rises to 10 to 99 years or life and a fine up to $100,000.
rows.issue: App merged two tiers: '>200g = 10 years to life, $100,000' is only true at 400 g or more; 200-399 g is 5-99 years/life with a $10,000 fine. Threshold should be split into 200-400g and >=400g rows.

rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.121(b)(1); Tex. Penal Code § 12.22
rows.notes: Texas has not legalized recreational marijuana. Possessing 2 ounces or less is a Class B misdemeanor: up to 180 days in jail and a fine up to $2,000.
rows.issue: Threshold should read '2 oz or less' (statute), not '<2oz'; values correct.

rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.121(b)(2); Tex. Penal Code § 12.21
rows.notes: Possessing more than 2 ounces up to 4 ounces of marijuana in Texas is a Class A misdemeanor: up to 1 year in jail and a fine up to $4,000.

rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.121(b)(3)-(6); Tex. Penal Code § 12.35
rows.notes: Possessing more than 4 ounces up to 5 pounds of marijuana in Texas is a state jail felony: 180 days to 2 years and a fine up to $10,000. Larger amounts are higher felonies: over 5 lb is third degree, over 50 lb second degree, over 2,000 lb first degree (5-99 years or life, up to $50,000).
rows.issue: Values only fit 4 oz-5 lb; row said '>4oz' with no upper limit, but over 5 lb is a third-degree felony or higher.

rows.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code § 481.115(b); Tex. Penal Code § 12.35
rows.notes: Possessing less than 1 gram of methamphetamine (Penalty Group 1) in Texas is a state jail felony: 180 days to 2 years and a fine up to $10,000.
rows.issue: Values confirmed from § 481.115(b); meth's listing in Penalty Group 1 (§ 481.102) was not re-read on the official page this pass.
